user_policy.application: Sliver framework implementation, including its operator commands and server RPC handlers, is hostile. Vendored third-party libraries, generic tests and content-free package fragments are judged by their isolated source bytes.
user_policy.hostile_evidence_counts: The network handler has three hostile findings in separate family/interface-query/connection-query directories. Each small monitor/licensing command has one precise hostile family finding: it has no additional independent hostile behavior to justify padding the count to three.
user_policy.scope_limit: The license command prints licenses, the monitor commands manage implant-intelligence monitoring, and the RPC server forwards queries. These are not labeled as implant payloads or as observed execution on a real endpoint.

methods: Inventoried and SHA-256-verified all 97 files. Read source, inspected library roles and code/API structure, and collected cleave facts for the core Sliver files and selected benign fragments.
Ran atomscan --format=json on all 97 samples before and after the changes, including archive children and decoded/compressed members.

Enumerated archive entries and inspected module declarations, READMEs, execution-related members and credential-handling paths. Safely decompressed the StackRox image JSON and located the exact false-positive match.
Ran cleave facts on selected extracted PostgreSQL administration, GPG, Kubernetes provisioning, Nix evaluation, database wizard and integration-test files.
Scanned neutral-path controls with renamed functions, import aliases, mismatched receivers/requests/modules, inert comments, notification methods and quoted JSON examples.
Validated a frozen snapshot, applied the reviewed Hopper assignments, independently verified all 97 assignments, and moved the 93 local benign copies without changing their bytes.

improvements.subject: Sliver server network queries
improvements.change: Recognizes protobuf request forwarding through the same RPC receiver, plus construction of the framework response envelope. Adds family identification and separate remote interface/connection-query observations.
improvements.generalization: Binds imported module aliases, request variables and receiver variables; does not require source filenames or local handler names.
improvements.placement: The response atom belongs in data/serialize/protobuf because it constructs a typed protocol message. It does not prove a transport operation or marshaling call.

improvements.subject: Sliver operator commands
improvements.change: Recognizes typed Sliver client usage, actual monitor RPC calls and the licensing-command callback reading the imported framework license collection.
improvements.generalization: Matches the real imported modules and type/API structure, including aliases and renamed local functions. Comments, unrelated modules, unrelated receivers and unrelated All members are negative controls.
improvements.limits: The current monitor matcher covers direct short-variable-assignment calls. The licensing matcher covers the observed Cobra Run callback construction. Other source structures remain outside these fingerprints.

improvements.subject: Neutral messaging capabilities
improvements.change: Adds eight observations for calls to SMS, text, message-posting, message-event, note-push and direct-message helpers.
improvements.generalization: Matches API-shaped calls without requiring caller variable names, provider hosts, credentials or attacker-specific strings.
improvements.limits: The descriptions identify helper calls; they do not prove the helper implementation, an external send, sensitive input, a C2 channel or exfiltration.

improvements.subject: JSON address substitution false positive
improvements.change: Separates source address-assignment syntax from actual unescaped JSON address properties, while retaining suspicious coverage for genuine JSON Ip/Interface shell-substitution values.
improvements.evidence: The old match was ip=\"$(dig inside a shell program quoted in StackRox image history, rather than an injected JSON address operand.
improvements.controls: Real nested JSON address/interface payloads and source-language payloads remain suspicious; plain addresses, escaped JSON examples and quoted shell history remain below suspicious.

atomscan.exit_note: The final batch returns 1 because findings are present; all 97 reports were produced.

make_validate_frozen.scope: Previously validated frozen Go review/improvement snapshot plus the 26 exact current files listed below. Unrelated concurrent workspace changes excluded.

make_validate_shared.status: seven unrelated concurrent Ruby/shell fixture failures

local_relocations.layout: Preserves each original uniquely named sample directory and its source-relative hierarchy. Historical __bad/__unknown collector suffixes remain directory provenance, not the corrected pool verdict.

limits: Static inspection, parsing and scanner checks only. No sample code, downloaded program, notification service, C2 endpoint, or installation hook was executed.

Archive analysis has source-local flow, unavailable-call/field and embedded-source gaps, counted per sample below. Review of a module archive is not proof that every dependency or every possible runtime path is benign.
The model reports feature spec v18 while the engine expects v21. No ML threshold or model was modified, and an ML score was not treated as proof of maliciousness.
Pool labels describe the isolated training artifacts. A benign third-party file found within a real Sliver deployment does not make that endpoint deployment safe.
